candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.10, Psychosocial Integrity — provide care and education for acute and chronic psychosocial health issues; use therapeutic communication and behavioral management techniques
candidate.educational_objective: For a client with schizophrenia who repeatedly stops medication, address adherence barriers and preferences and recognize a long-acting injectable as an appropriate option when preferred or when adherence is poor or uncertain.

options.A: Explore why the client stops treatment, discuss benefits, adverse effects and preferences, and collaborate with the prescriber about a long-acting injectable if the client prefers it or adherence remains poor or uncertain.
options.B: Increase the antipsychotic dose automatically whenever the client reports feeling better, even when there is no evidence that the prescribed dose is ineffective.
options.C: Avoid discussing adverse effects because acknowledging medication problems generally makes clients less willing to continue treatment.
options.D: Postpone adherence planning until another relapse occurs because symptom improvement means maintenance antipsychotic treatment is no longer needed.

candidate.rationale: APA guidance recommends continuing antipsychotic treatment after symptoms improve and specifically suggests a long-acting injectable antipsychotic when a patient prefers it or has a history of poor or uncertain adherence. Treatment planning should remain patient-centered and adverse effects should be monitored rather than ignored. Therefore A is the best strategy. B changes dose without a clinical indication, C conflicts with monitoring and shared treatment planning, and D delays intervention despite an established adherence problem.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Patients whose schizophrenia symptoms improve should continue antipsychotic treatment; a long-acting injectable may be used when preferred or when adherence is poor or uncertain.
candidate.source_document_title: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia, Third Edition
